# Hamiltonian-first: dispersion generated by the invariant Theta symplectic form

**Conditional C-tier theorem, 2026-10-24.** Uses the candidate pointwise 2-form Ω(X,Y)=B(X,JY) from draft #717; no new field, no gravitational action, no claim this is the uniquely selected physical Hamiltonian.

Let JX=iX, J²=-1, B symmetric, nondegenerate, J-compatible with inertia (2,6). On a **fixed spatial manifold with prescribed time-independent positive density and boundary conditions**, use the formal symplectic form ∫Ω(δX,δX) and Hamiltonian candidate
\[
H_{c,m}[X]=\frac12\int_\Sigma \mu\,[c\,h^{ij}B(D_iX,D_jX)+m^2B(X,X)].
\]
Here h, μ, D_i, c and m² are *trial data*, not derived UBT parameters. Assume D_i preserves B and J and admits integration by parts without boundary flux. Define A=-c D_i^\ast D^i+m² with the sign convention \(\delta H(Y)=\int\mu B(AX,Y)\), so for flat ordinary derivatives \(A=-c\Delta+m²\). From \(\iota_{\dot X}\Omega=dH\) one obtains
\[
\boxed{\partial_tX=JAX=i(-c\Delta+m²)X}\quad\text{(flat fixed background)}.
\]
For X=u e^{i(k\cdot x+\omega t)} with real wavevector, \(\omega=c|k|²+m²\) on the stated convention. **It is first order in time with quadratic spatial dispersion**, not the relativistic Klein–Gordon/wave relation \(\omega²=|k|²+m²\). One cannot identify this trial as a Lorentz-covariant fundamental time generator merely because its internal symmetries are invariant.

More generally any differentiable *local algebraic* Hamiltonian density f(I), I=B(X,X)/2, yields \(\dot X=f'(I)JX\) at fixed spatial point (with the same compatible measures/conventions). Since \(\dot I=B(X,\dot X)=0\), this is amplitude-dependent internal phase rotation, no spatial transport. Spatial derivatives are necessary for this choice of symplectic form to propagate modes, but not sufficient to obtain relativistic dispersion.

**Energy caveat:** since B has inertia (2,6), positive c and m² do not make this unconstrained trial Hamiltonian bounded below. Gauge reduction/constraints could change this but have not been derived. No inference about gravity, cosmology, or positivity is justified.

**Action gate:** A first-order-in-time symplectic phase-space action can be *written* once Ω,H are chosen, but doing so would only rewrite the candidates, not derive UBT's fundamental action. Need a selector for the physical Poisson structure, evolution in τ=t+iψ, and the constraint generators whose closure yields spacetime covariance. Do not identify \(i\partial_t\) with a \(\psi\)-derivative without an explicit analyticity/reality theorem.
